kit.name: ELEGOO UNO R3 Most Complete Starter Kit

identity.manufacturer: Generic; no brand name is printed on ELEGOO's board. This is the same widely cloned design sold by many Chinese module makers under the name KY-038.
identity.manufacturer_part_number: Not confirmed for ELEGOO's exact board; commonly sold industry-wide as KY-038
identity.package: module: small PCB with an upright electret microphone (a tiny microphone capsule that needs no separate power to pick up sound), a blue trimmer potentiometer, and a 4-pin header

function.one_sentence_plain_english: A small board with a tiny microphone that tells the Arduino how loud the sound around it is, and can also just say yes or no once it gets loud enough.
function.what_it_is_used_for: Detecting sound or loudness, for example a clap-activated switch, a noise alarm, or any sound-triggered project.
function.how_it_works_briefly: The microphone turns sound into a tiny voltage. An onboard amplifier boosts that signal, which comes out on the AO (analog output) pin as a continuously changing voltage. A comparator circuit (a chip that checks whether one voltage is bigger than another) compares the amplified signal to a threshold set by the blue trimmer potentiometer (a small adjustable resistor you turn with a screwdriver); when the sound crosses that threshold, the DO (digital output) pin flips between high and low.

pinout.name: VCC
pinout.notes: 3.3V to 5V, per the robotpishop.com listing for this class of module; ELEGOO's own tutorial does not state a supply figure

pinout.name: DO
pinout.notes: Goes high or low once the sound crosses the threshold set by the onboard potentiometer (ELEGOO tutorial)

pinout.name: AO
pinout.notes: Continuous voltage signal following the microphone in real time (ELEGOO tutorial)

pins.pin_1_identification: Not confirmed from a source with a labeled photo of ELEGOO's exact board. The tutorial names the 4 signals (VCC, GND, DO, AO) and how to wire them, but does not show their left-to-right physical order on the header. Read the small printed letters next to each pin on the board itself rather than assuming an order.

electrical.operating_voltage: 3.3V to 5V DC (robotpishop.com retailer listing for this module design)
electrical.absolute_max_voltage: not confirmed from a source I fetched
electrical.typical_current: not confirmed from a source I fetched
electrical.max_current: not confirmed from a source I fetched
electrical.logic_level: not explicitly confirmed; DO is a simple on/off digital signal that should be safe to read directly on an UNO's 5V-logic input pins

key_specs.microphone_type: electret condenser microphone (a small, cheap microphone that does not need its own separate power supply)
key_specs.signal_path: microphone, then an onboard amplifier, then a peak detector and buffer feeding the AO pin; a separate comparator stage drives DO (ELEGOO tutorial's own description)
key_specs.sensitivity_adjustment: adjustable via the onboard blue trimmer potentiometer; ELEGOO's tutorial notes it takes at least 10 full turns to see a response, since it is a fine-adjustment part
key_specs.indicator_leds: one LED shows the board has power, a second LED lights when the digital threshold is tripped (ELEGOO tutorial)

visual_identification.shape_and_size: Small rectangular green PCB, roughly 3 to 4 cm long, with a small round metal-cased microphone capsule standing upright on one end
visual_identification.color_and_markings: Green PCB; a small blue square trimmer potentiometer near the microphone; two small LEDs on the board
visual_identification.printed_text_to_look_for: Look for the letters 'AO' and 'DO' printed near the header pins, and a round metal microphone can with a small sound-entry hole in its top face
easily_confused_with: KY-037 high-sensitivity sound sensor (very similar board layout)
other small electret microphone breakout boards

wiring_to_uno.arduino_library: None required; ELEGOO's Lesson 20 example sketch uses only the built-in analogRead and digitalRead functions

hazards: None significant; low voltage sensor module
handling_notes: Avoid touching or blocking the microphone's sound-entry hole
The sensitivity potentiometer needs many turns to change anything; adjust it slowly with a small screwdriver
common_mistakes: Expecting DO to respond to normal-volume sound before turning the threshold potentiometer down
Swapping the AO and DO wires

symptoms_and_causes.likely_cause: Threshold potentiometer set too high for the ambient sound level
symptoms_and_causes.check: Per ELEGOO's tutorial, turn the potentiometer counter-clockwise until the indicator LED goes out, then turn it back slowly while making noise

symptoms_and_causes.symptom: AO reads a constant flat value
symptoms_and_causes.likely_cause: Microphone or amplifier fault, or AO and DO wires swapped
symptoms_and_causes.check: Confirm AO is wired to an analog pin (A0 to A5) and DO to a digital pin

troubleshooting.how_to_test_with_a_multimeter: With VCC and GND connected and the module powered, measure DC voltage at AO; it should sit a small fraction of a volt above 0V at rest and jump briefly when you make a sudden loud sound near the microphone.

typical_suppliers: Amazon (usually sold in packs of 4 to 5)

confidence.notes: ELEGOO does not publish a standalone spec sheet for this module. Everything beyond what ELEGOO's own tutorial states is corroborated from the widely sold KY-038 module design, which behaves the same way (AO analog out, DO digital out through an onboard comparator and potentiometer) but was not visually confirmed to be bit-for-bit identical to ELEGOO's exact board. This module is confirmed present in the current EL-KIT-001 kit.
